reflection: Results are not visible in this run, so I am relying on the notebook of formulas and the stated feature importances. Volatility (10d, 20d), MSFT_return_1d and NVDA 5d returns carried most signal. I will build on those: volatility-regime variants and peer-lead factors with new constructions. I will avoid repeating earlier formulas and keep the formulas simple and robust.

lessons.name: aapl_vol10_to_vol60_ratio
lessons.lesson: Vol regime ratio is related to the top existing factor (vol10), so it may be partly redundant but captures mean-reverting volatility.

lessons.name: msft_return_zscore_20d
lessons.lesson: Standardising MSFT's move may help across volatility regimes but is highly correlated with MSFT_return_1d.

lessons.name: aapl_overnight_gap
lessons.lesson: Overnight gap is mostly noise for next-day direction unless combined with the prior trend.

lessons.name: aapl_close_location_in_range
lessons.lesson: Close location is a weak one-day reversal/continuation signal and noisy alone.

lessons.name: qqq_vol_ratio_5_20
lessons.lesson: Market vol-shift is a plausible regime marker but unsigned, so its direction effect is weak.

lessons.name: aapl_minus_msft_5d_relative
lessons.lesson: Relative 5d strength could mean-revert but scale changes across years weaken it.

lessons.name: aapl_close_location_avg_3d
lessons.lesson: Smoothing reduces noise but the signal is still weak.

lessons.name: aapl_minus_msft_5d_vol_scaled
lessons.lesson: Vol scaling fixes cross-year scale but adds ratio noise.

lessons.name: aapl_intraday_return
lessons.lesson: Intraday return mostly duplicates the 1d return so it adds little.

lessons.name: peer_dispersion_1d
lessons.lesson: Unsigned dispersion has no direction, needs a partner for sign.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_trend_signed
lessons.lesson: Volume times sign is noisy and the volume scale shifts with time.

lessons.name: qqq_trend_vs_aapl_gap_20d
lessons.lesson: Long-horizon relative gaps overlap heavily with the existing 20d return.

lessons.name: aapl_minus_msft_5d_vol_scaled_z
lessons.lesson: Double normalisation probably over-smooths and loses signal.

lessons.name: qqq_vol_ratio_5_60_signed
lessons.lesson: Signed vol ratio is a convoluted interaction and probably noisy.

lessons.name: aapl_range_expansion_z
lessons.lesson: Range z-score is a volatility proxy that overlaps existing vol factors.

lessons.name: nvda_minus_qqq_3d_lead
lessons.lesson: NVDA leadership is plausible but 3d smoothing blurs the lead signal.

lessons.name: aapl_gap_vs_qqq_gap
lessons.lesson: Gap differences are small and noisy.

factors.name: aapl_vol10_to_vol60_ratio_log
factors.hypothesis: The raw ratio is skewed, which hurts LR. A log makes it symmetric and keeps the vol-regime information of the top factor.

factors.name: msft_return_vol_scaled_1d
factors.hypothesis: A 60d vol scale is steadier than the 20d z-score, which was noisy, so MSFT's move is comparable across regimes.

factors.name: qqq_down_day_streak_pressure
factors.hypothesis: Summed absolute QQQ moves over 5d measure how turbulent the market is, which should relate to Apple's next-day behaviour.

factors.name: aapl_high_low_vs_close_pressure
factors.hypothesis: The distance of the close from the range midpoint, scaled by price, is a one-day pressure measure. A close near the low often precedes a bounce.

factors.name: aapl_ret_minus_nvda_msft_lag1_gap
factors.hypothesis: This is a short relative-strength measure. It complements the vol regime by showing whether Apple lags or leads when volatility is high or low.

factors.name: nvda_vol_scaled_lead_5d
factors.hypothesis: This is NVDA's 5d move scaled by its own volatility, a tech risk-appetite state. It gives MSFT's daily move context, since the shuffle test ranked NVDA 5d as important.
